title: Operation Valkyrie & The Plot To Kill Hitler
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 出品的《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在这里，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上稀奇古怪、美妙绝伦的事情，同时还能提高英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about Operation Valkyrie and the plot to assassinate Hitler.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们要聊的是“瓦尔基里行动”（Operation Valkyrie）以及刺杀希特勒的阴谋。

sentences.en: It’s a story of bombs, plots, secret briefcases, underground bunkers, and one of history’s greatest “what ifs”.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于炸弹、密谋、秘密公文包、地下掩体以及历史上最大“如果”之一的故事。

sentences.en: OK then, let's not waste a minute and get right into it.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们废话少说，马上切入正题。

sentences.en: In the early afternoon of July 20th, 1944, twenty or so senior Nazi officials were gathered around a long oak table in the Wolf’s Lair, Hitler’s military headquarters on the Eastern Front, in modern-day Poland.
sentences.zh: 1944年7月20日刚过正午，大约二十名纳粹高级官员聚集在“狼穴”（Wolf’s Lair）的一张长橡木桌旁，这里是希特勒在东线（位于今天的波兰）的军事总部。

sentences.en: The situation for the Nazi war machine was getting worse by the day.
sentences.zh: 纳粹战争机器的局势一天比一天糟糕。

sentences.en: The Allies had landed in Normandy six weeks earlier, Russia was advancing on the Eastern Front, the Allies had captured Rome, and the United States was advancing towards Japan.
sentences.zh: 盟军在六周前登陆诺曼底，苏联军队在东线步步推进，盟军占领了罗马，美国也正向日本推进。

sentences.en: If the war was still winnable for Nazi Germany, well, it would take something very special.
sentences.zh: 如果纳粹德国还要赢得这场战争，嗯，那得发生点极其不寻常的事才行。

sentences.en: A meeting had been called, and senior Nazi leaders had been instructed to fly in for it.
sentences.zh: 当时召集了一场会议，并已指示纳粹高层官员乘机前来参加。

sentences.en: One such officer was Claus von Stauffenberg, a 36-year-old Lieutenant Colonel who had been awarded the Iron Cross for his bravery in the Battle of France.
sentences.zh: 其中一位军官是克劳斯·冯·施陶芬贝格（Claus von Stauffenberg），他是一名36岁的中校，曾在法兰西战役中因英勇表现而被授予铁十字勋章。

sentences.en: Von Stauffenberg knew all too well the cost of war; he had been fighting in North Africa, where he had lost an eye, his entire right hand, and two fingers on his left.
sentences.zh: 冯·施陶芬贝格对战争的代价有着切身体会；他曾在北非作战，在那里他失去了一只眼睛、整个右手以及左手上的两根手指。

sentences.en: It had taken him three months to recover, but he was still without one eye and seven fingers, so he was transferred to office duty, far from the front line.
sentences.zh: 他花了三个月的时间才康复，但仍然少了一只眼睛和七根手指，因此他被调到了远离前线的文职岗位。

sentences.en: He had met Hitler on several occasions, and Hitler had always been polite and courteous to him; after all, the sacrifices this man had made for the Nazi cause were plain to see.
sentences.zh: 他曾多次见过希特勒，希特勒对他也总是彬彬有礼、客客气气；毕竟，这个人为了纳粹事业所做出的牺牲是有目共睹的。

sentences.en: So when von Stauffenberg arrived a couple of minutes late for the meeting, instead of receiving a dressing down and being shouted at by the Führer, there was a quiet nod of acceptance.
sentences.zh: 因此，当冯·施陶芬贝格迟到几分钟到达会场时，并没有遭到元首的训斥和咆哮，而是得到了一下表示默许的平静点头。

sentences.en: Indeed, von Stauffenberg had only arrived at the Wolf’s Lair that morning.
sentences.zh: 事实上，冯·施陶芬贝格那天早上才刚抵达“狼穴”。

sentences.en: He would have been on time for the meeting, but it was such a hot day and he was drenched in sweat.
sentences.zh: 他本来是可以按时开会的，但天气实在太热，他大汗淋漓。

sentences.en: He had to go and change his shirt, and he needed his assistant to help him.
sentences.zh: 他不得不去换件衬衫，而且需要助手帮忙。

sentences.en: After all, belts, buckles, and buttons, they aren’t so simple if you are only operating with three fingers.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，如果只有三根手指能用，皮带、扣子和纽扣处理起来可没那么简单。

sentences.en: The meeting was to be held in a different room from usual; normally, these types of meetings were held deep underground, in reinforced concrete bunkers.
sentences.zh: 当天的会议将在一个与以往不同的房间举行；通常，这类会议都在深埋地下的钢筋混凝土掩体中举行。

sentences.en: But it was so hot that nobody would have lasted very long down there, without any ventilation.
sentences.zh: 但当时天气太热，如果没有通风设备，谁也无法在下面待太久。

sentences.en: So the meeting was taking place above ground, with the windows open for fresh air.
sentences.zh: 所以会议改在地面上举行，窗户大开着呼吸新鲜空气。

sentences.en: Von Stauffenberg had been ushered into a room next to the conference room to allow him to get changed in private.
sentences.zh: 冯·施陶芬贝格被领进会议室旁的一个房间，以便他能私下更衣。

sentences.en: Together with his assistant, the pair proceeded to open up the briefcase.
sentences.zh: 他和助手一起打开了公文包。

sentences.en: They took out the spare shirt, but they were more interested in what the shirt was wrapped around: two sticks of plastic explosives, two bombs.
sentences.zh: 他们拿出了备用衬衫，但他们更关心的是衬衫包裹的东西：两根塑胶炸药，也就是两枚炸弹。

sentences.en: The men began to prime the device, setting a timer for 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 两人开始给装置引信，设置了一个10分钟的定时器。

sentences.en: They completed the first, but before the men had the chance to prime the second bomb, there was a knock on the door: “What are you up to in there?
sentences.zh: 他们完成了第一个，但还没等两人来得及给第二个炸弹装信管，门就被敲响了：“你在里面干什么呢？

sentences.en: Quick, the meeting is about to begin.” There were assurances that they’d be out in a minute; von Stauffenberg was just having a bit of trouble with his belt.
sentences.zh: 快点，会议马上就要开始了。”他们保证说马上就出来；冯·施陶芬贝格只是皮带出了点小问题。

sentences.en: And sure enough, shortly after, the door opened.
sentences.zh: 果不其然，不久之后，门打开了。

sentences.en: Von Stauffenberg was there in a new shirt, briefcase in hand.
sentences.zh: 冯·施陶芬贝格换了一件新衬衫站在那里，手里拿着公文包。

sentences.en: He was ushered into the conference room, where the meeting was already in full flow.
sentences.zh: 他被领进了正在进行中的会议室。

sentences.en: Hitler was standing in the middle, leaning over a map placed on the table.
sentences.zh: 希特勒正站在中央，俯身看着桌上的一张地图。

sentences.en: Von Stauffenberg approached the table and slid the briefcase underneath, next to where Hitler was standing.
sentences.zh: 冯·施陶芬贝格走近桌子，把公文包塞在桌子下面，挨着希特勒站立的地方。

sentences.en: A couple of minutes later, an attendant came in and knocked von Stauffenberg on the shoulder: Sir, there’s a telephone call for you.
sentences.zh: 几分钟后，一名随从进来拍了拍冯·施陶芬贝格的肩膀：长官，有您的电话。

sentences.en: Von Stauffenberg made his excuses and left the room.
sentences.zh: 冯·施陶芬贝格找了个借口离开了房间。

sentences.en: At 12.42, just a few minutes after von Stauffenberg’s departure, there was a massive explosion right in the heart of the Wolf’s Lair.
sentences.zh: 12点42分，就在冯·施陶芬贝格离开几分钟后，“狼穴”的正中心发生了一场大爆炸。

sentences.en: It looked like it might even have come from the conference room itself.
sentences.zh: 看起来甚至像是直接从会议室里传出来的。

sentences.en: By this point, von Stauffenberg was making a beeline for the perimeter, heading for the exit as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，冯·施陶芬贝格正直奔警戒线，以最快速度赶往出口。

sentences.en: It’s not known exactly what he told the guards to be allowed through the numerous checkpoints that surrounded the Wolf’s Lair, but by 1 pm, less than 20 minutes after the blast, von Stauffenberg and his assistant were on an aeroplane back to Berlin.
sentences.zh: 目前还不清楚他究竟对卫兵说了什么才得以通过包围“狼穴”的众多检查站，但到了下午1点，即爆炸发生不到20分钟后，冯·施陶芬贝格和他的助手就已经坐上了返回柏林的飞机。

sentences.en: The hard part was done. Adolf Hitler was dead, and a bunch of his senior leadership too.
sentences.zh: 最困难的部分已经完成了。阿道夫·希特勒死了，他的一帮高层领导也死了。

sentences.en: The next part was, comparatively, easy: mobilise the emergency “continuity of government” plan, appoint an interim successor, and most probably seek peace with the Allies.
sentences.zh: 接下来的一部分相对来说就容易了：启动紧急“政府延续”计划，任命一个临时接班人，并且极有可能是向盟军寻求和平。

sentences.en: The only problem was…Hitler wasn’t dead.
sentences.zh: 唯一的问题是……希特勒没死。

sentences.en: Unbeknownst to von Stauffenberg, his carefully positioned briefcase had been slightly pushed to one side, tucked behind the leg of the heavy oak conference table.
sentences.zh: 冯·施陶芬贝格并不知道，他精心放置的公文包被稍微推向了一边，塞到了厚重橡木会议桌桌腿的后面。

sentences.en: Most probably, this was done by an officer called Heinz Brandt, who just pushed the briefcase with his feet, not out of any great patriotic duty, but because it was in the way of where he wanted to put his legs.
sentences.zh: 极有可能是海因茨·勃兰特（Heinz Brandt）这位军官做的，他用脚把公文包踢到了一边，倒不是出于什么伟大的爱国主义责任，而是因为它挡住了他想放脚的地方。

sentences.en: It might well have been the act that saved Hitler’s life, but it cost Brandt his: he died the following day, one of the four people in the conference room to die from the blast.
sentences.zh: 这很可能是救了希特勒一命的举动，但却要了勃兰特的命：他在第二天去世，是会议室里因爆炸身亡的四人之一。

sentences.en: Another nine were seriously injured, and the remaining eleven escaped with minor injuries.
sentences.zh: 另有九人重伤，其余十一人受轻伤。

sentences.en: And this included the target of the entire operation: Adolf Hitler.
sentences.zh: 这其中就包括整个行动的目标：阿道夫·希特勒。

sentences.en: His trousers were torn to shreds, his arm was damaged, and his eardrum burst.
sentences.zh: 他的裤子被炸成了碎片，手臂受伤，耳膜破裂。

sentences.en: But he survived. In the immediate aftermath of the event, he could be seen wandering around the rubble, inspecting the chaos.
sentences.zh: 但他活了下来。事件发生后不久，人们可以看到他在废墟中四处徘徊，查看混乱的现场。

sentences.en: Officers tried to understand what had happened.
sentences.zh: 军官们试图弄清楚发生了什么。

sentences.en: Had a Soviet bomber flown overhead and dropped a bomb with such precision that it landed in the exact conference room where the Führer had been meeting?
sentences.zh: 难道是苏联轰炸机从头顶飞过，投下了一颗极其精准的炸弹，正好落在了元首开会的那个会议室里？

sentences.en: No, no planes had been seen, and there were no other explosions.
sentences.zh: 不，没有看到飞机，也没有发生其他爆炸。

sentences.en: The focus quickly switched to a threat from within, and suspicion fell on the man who had entered with a briefcase, then quickly left without one: Lieutenant Colonel von Stauffenberg.
sentences.zh: 焦点迅速转移到来自内部的威胁，怀疑落在了那个提着公文包进来、随后又空手迅速离开的人身上：中校冯·施陶芬贝格。

sentences.en: By this point, von Stauffenberg was in the air, on the way back to Berlin.
sentences.zh: 此时，冯·施陶芬贝格正在返回柏林的空中。

sentences.en: By the time he landed, he expected Operation Valkyrie to be well underway.
sentences.zh: 当他降落时，他本以为“瓦尔基里行动”已经在紧锣密鼓地进行了。

sentences.en: Now, Operation Valkyrie was the codename for the operation that would be triggered if there was a full breakdown of civic order in Nazi Germany, or if there was some kind of uprising from the foreign workers in German factories.
sentences.zh: 现在，“瓦尔基里行动”是一个代号，如果纳粹德国的公民秩序彻底崩溃，或者德国工厂里的外国工人发生某种暴动，该行动就会被触发。

sentences.en: It was essentially a plan that would see the territorial reserve army seize control of the streets and key state functions.
sentences.zh: 它本质上是一项由本土后备军接管街道和国家核心职能的计划。

sentences.en: Importantly, Operation Valkyrie wasn’t a secret plot.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，“瓦尔基里行动”并不是一个秘密阴谋。

sentences.en: It had been drawn up as a genuine emergency plan to crush unrest or uprisings, and Hitler himself even signed off on it.
sentences.zh: 它是作为镇压骚乱或起义的真正紧急计划而起草的，希特勒本人甚至还签署批准了它。

sentences.en: But unbeknownst to Hitler, Operation Valkyrie was being used to take him down.
sentences.zh: 但希特勒不知道的是，“瓦尔基里行动”正被用来推翻他。

sentences.en: It was a clever idea in theory. Kill Hitler, declare that he had been assassinated by rogue, rebel forces within the Nazi party, namely the SS.
sentences.zh: 理论上这是一个聪明的想法。杀死希特勒，宣布他是被纳粹党内部的分裂反叛势力（即党卫军）暗杀的。

sentences.en: Arrest these supposedly rogue forces, declare martial law, and declare a Field Marshall called Erwin von Witzleben as Commander in Chief.
sentences.zh: 逮捕这些所谓的反叛势力，宣布戒严，并宣布一位名叫埃尔温·冯·维茨莱本（Erwin von Witzleben）的元帅为总司令。

sentences.en: It was a clever idea because it would pin all blame on the SS and “treacherous forces within the Nazi party”, allowing for a relatively smooth transition to a Hitler-free Germany without all of the mess that might come from a more overt coup or assassination attempt.
sentences.zh: 这是一个聪明的想法，因为它会将所有的责任归咎于党卫军和“纳粹党内的叛国势力”，从而相对顺利地过渡到一个没有希特勒的德国，而不会产生通过更公开的政变或暗杀企图可能带来的所有混乱。

sentences.en: And, after all, this was far from the only attempt on Hitler’s life.
sentences.zh: 而且，毕竟这绝不是唯一一次谋杀希特勒的企图。

sentences.en: There are 42 documented assassination attempts, with presumably many more than this that were never discovered.
sentences.zh: 有记录的暗杀企图就有42次，据推测还有更多从未被发现的暗杀。

sentences.en: From poisoned letters to bombs to snipers, starting in 1932, all manner of methods and locations were tried.
sentences.zh: 从毒信到炸弹再到狙击手，从1932年开始，各种方法和地点都尝试过了。

sentences.en: Miraculously, Hitler survived all of them.
sentences.zh: 不可思议的是，希特勒在所有暗杀中都活了下来。

sentences.en: But it was this attempt, the attempt of the 20th of July, 1944, which was the widest reaching, the best planned, and perhaps came closest to succeeding.
sentences.zh: 但正是这次企图——1944年7月20日的企图，是波及面最广、策划最周密、而且最接近成功的一次。

sentences.en: Now, it’s unclear exactly how many people were involved in the plot, and what knowledge different people had of its inner workings.
sentences.zh: 目前还不清楚具体有多少人参与了这个阴谋，以及不同的人对它的内部运作了解多少。

sentences.en: What is clear is that there had been various groups within the Nazi upper leadership that had been planning to overthrow or kill Hitler since before the start of the war.
sentences.zh: 但明确的是，早在战争爆发之前，纳粹高层领导层内部就一直有各种团体在策划推翻或杀死希特勒。

sentences.en: And as for their intentions, well, they were varied.
sentences.zh: 至于他们的动机，嗯，可以说是形形色色。

sentences.en: Those directly involved in the July 20th plot included nationalists, democrats, aristocrats and communists.
sentences.zh: 直接参与7月20日阴谋的人包括民族主义者、民主主义者、贵族和共产主义者。

sentences.en: This wasn’t one homogenous group with a clear, unified aim for post-Hitler Germany, nor is it fair to characterise them as some great upstanding group of moral citizens who were disgusted by the behaviour of the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个有着清晰、统一目标的战后德国愿景的同质化群体，把他们描述为对纳粹行为感到厌恶的伟大高尚道德公民群体也是不公平的。

sentences.en: For some, this might well have been the case.
sentences.zh: 对某些人来说，情况可能确实如此。

sentences.en: In von Stauffenberg’s case, several historians have suggested that he had a strong moral objection to the treatment of Jews.
sentences.zh: 就冯·施陶芬贝格而言，几位历史学家指出他对犹太人的待遇有着强烈的道义反对。

sentences.en: For many other military officers, though, the motivation was more pragmatic.
sentences.zh: 然而，对于许多其他军官来说，动机更多是出于实用主义。

sentences.en: The disasters at Stalingrad in 1943, the Allied landings in Normandy in June 1944, and the rapid Soviet advance on the Eastern Front convinced them the war was lost under Hitler’s leadership.
sentences.zh: 1943年的斯大林格勒灾难、1944年6月的盟军诺曼底登陆以及苏联在东线的迅速推进，让他们坚信在希特勒的领导下战争已经输定了。

sentences.en: It was a motley crew, but what did unite them was a firm belief that Adolf Hitler needed to be removed from power, and killing him and pinning the blame on “rebel factions” was the best way of doing it.
sentences.zh: 这是一群乌合之众，但将他们团结在一起的是一种坚定的信念：必须将阿道夫·希特勒赶下台，而杀死他并将罪名归咎于“反叛派系”是实现这一目标的最佳途径。

sentences.en: So, when von Stauffenberg touched down in Berlin and made his way to the army headquarters, he was expecting to hear that Operation Valkyrie was in full swing: Hitler was dead, the reserve army units had taken control of the key state institutions, and the groups most loyal to Hitler, in particular the SS, had been neutralised.
sentences.zh: 因此，当冯·施陶芬贝格在柏林降落并前往陆军总部时，他本期待听到“瓦尔基里行动”正在全速进行：希特勒已死，后备军部队已经接管了国家核心机构，而最忠于希特勒的群体（特别是党卫军）已经被消灭。

sentences.en: But he soon realised that things weren’t going as smoothly as he had hoped and that, in fact, there was a potentially devastating problem.
sentences.zh: 但他很快意识到事情并没有像他希望的那样顺利，事实上，有一个潜在的毁灭性问题。

sentences.en: There had been a phone call from the Wolf’s Lair to the plotters at central command confirming that there had been a massive explosion in the conference room, but the message that came through was that Hitler had survived.
sentences.zh: 狼穴曾给中央指挥部的密谋者打过电话，确认会议室发生了大爆炸，但传过来的消息是希特勒活了下来。

sentences.en: And if Hitler wasn’t dead, then the whole thing came crashing down.
sentences.zh: 如果希特勒没死，那么整盘计划就会彻底崩溃。

sentences.en: For Operation Valkyrie to work, the reserve army units had to buy the lie that Hitler had been killed by disloyal forces within the Nazi party, and that was the reason the crackdown was necessary.
sentences.zh: 要让“瓦尔基里行动”发挥作用，后备军部队必须相信“希特勒是被纳粹党内部不忠势力杀害的”这个谎言，这也是必须进行清洗的原因。

sentences.en: At first, von Stauffenberg insisted, “I saw the explosion.
sentences.zh: 起初，冯·施陶芬贝格坚称：“我看到了爆炸。

sentences.en: Nobody could have survived it. Hitler is dead.”
sentences.zh: 没有人能活下来。希特勒死了。”

sentences.en: So the plotters had these two contradicting reports: von Stauffenberg saying Hitler is dead, and the other saying he isn’t.
sentences.zh: 于是密谋者们得到了这两个相互矛盾的报告：冯·施陶芬贝格说希特勒死了，而另一条说他没死。

sentences.en: Finally, at 4 pm that afternoon, the order was given to put Operation Valkyrie into action.
sentences.zh: 最后，当天下午4点，下达了启动“瓦尔基里行动”的命令。

sentences.en: Radio messages were sent to major military centres, and across Berlin, and in military districts throughout Germany, reserve army units were mobilised.
sentences.zh: 电报发往了各大军事中心、整个柏林以及德国各地的军事区，后备军部队被动员起来。

sentences.en: They began arresting local SS officers, seizing key government buildings, and preparing proclamations to the German people.
sentences.zh: 他们开始逮捕当地的党卫军军官，接管关键政府大楼，并准备向德国人民发表公告。

sentences.en: For a few tense hours that afternoon, it looked as though the coup might actually succeed.
sentences.zh: 那天下午在几个紧张的小时里，政变似乎真的有可能成功。

sentences.en: And let’s remember, these reserve troops don’t know that they are part of a coup; they are simply following their orders, which are to put into place this contingency plan, which involves rooting out treacherous elements within the Nazi party.
sentences.zh: 让我们记住，这些后备预备部队并不知道自己是一场政变的一部分；他们只是在执行命令，即落实这项应急计划，其中包含清除纳粹党内的叛国分子。

sentences.en: They even manage to detain Joseph Goebbels, the Nazi propaganda chief, in his Berlin office.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至设法在柏林办公室里扣押了纳粹宣传头子约瑟夫·戈培尔（Joseph Goebbels）。

sentences.en: Goebbels has realised it’s a coup, and knows the one thing he can do to stop it: make sure the reservists know that Hitler isn’t dead.
sentences.zh: 戈培尔已经意识到这是一场政变，并且知道阻止它的唯一方法：确保预备役军人知道希特勒没死。

sentences.en: So when he is detained by Major Otto Ernst Remer, a commanding officer of the reserve troops, Goebbels puts Hitler on the line.
sentences.zh: 因此，当他被预备役部队指挥官奥托·恩斯特·雷默（Otto Ernst Remer）少校扣押时，戈培尔直接把希特勒的电话接了进来。

sentences.en: Major Remer now realises that he has been duped, and he listens for his orders.
sentences.zh: 雷默少校现在意识到自己被愚弄了，他听从了指示。

sentences.en: Crush the plot, he is told, and take them alive.
sentences.zh: 他被告知：粉碎阴谋，并活捉他们。

sentences.en: It’s around 7 o’clock in the evening at this point, and the conspirators are in disarray.
sentences.zh: 此时大约是傍晚7点，阴谋分子陷入了混乱。

sentences.en: General Friedrich Fromm, the commander in chief of the reserve army, had been aware of the plot and had done nothing to stop it, essentially making him a conspirator and aide to the coup.
sentences.zh: 后备军总司令弗里德里希·弗罗姆（Friedrich Fromm）将军此前一直知晓这个阴谋却没有阻止，这实质上使他成为了政变阴谋者和帮凶。

sentences.en: But when it became clear that the bomb hadn’t done its job, he quickly started to cover his tracks, switching sides.
sentences.zh: 但当炸弹没有发挥预期作用变得明朗时，他迅速开始掩盖行踪，临阵倒戈。

sentences.en: He even tries to have von Stauffenberg arrested.
sentences.zh: 他甚至试图逮捕冯·施陶芬贝格。

sentences.en: Chaos breaks out. There was a firefight at the Bendlerblock, the Berlin headquarters where several of the conspirators were based, and von Stauffenberg was shot in the arm.
sentences.zh: 混乱爆发了。在柏林总部本德勒布洛克（Bendlerblock，许多阴谋分子的大本营）发生了一场枪战，冯·施陶芬贝格的手臂中枪。

sentences.en: By 11 pm that evening, the tide had well and truly turned.
sentences.zh: 到了当晚11点，局势彻底逆转。

sentences.en: The Bendlerblock was surrounded, and the reserve army managed to overpower the plotters.
sentences.zh: 本德勒布洛克被包围，后备军成功制服了密谋者。

sentences.en: General Fromm pushed for an impromptu court to be set up to try the conspirators, and he then court-martialled four of the conspirators, including von Stauffenberg, who were taken into the courtyard and shot.
sentences.zh: 弗罗姆将军力主成立一个临时法庭来审判密谋者，随后他将包括冯·施陶芬贝格在内的四名密谋者交付军事法庭审判，他们被带到庭院枪决。

sentences.en: Presumably, Fromm rushed this through, despite Hitler’s express order for the conspirators not to be executed, so that they couldn’t reveal his involvement in the plot.
sentences.zh: 大概是因为弗罗姆不顾希特勒严禁处决密谋者的明令，急忙将他们处决，好让他们无法供出他参与阴谋的事实。

sentences.en: Or, as Goebbels neatly put it, “You have been in a damn hurry to get your witnesses below ground."
sentences.zh: 或者，正如戈培尔精辟地说的那样：“你们可真够着急把证人送进地底下的。”

sentences.en: The entire coup, or attempted coup, lasted less than 12 hours.
sentences.zh: 整场政变，或者说未遂政变，持续了不到12小时。

sentences.en: And the aftermath was brutal. Over the following weeks, the Gestapo uncovered thousands of people connected, or suspected of being connected, to the conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 其后的清洗极其残酷。在接下来的几周里，盖世太保逮捕了数千名与阴谋有关或涉嫌有关的人。

sentences.en: Show trials were held in the People’s Court, presided over by the raging, screaming judge Roland Freisler.
sentences.zh: 公开审判在人民法院举行，由暴怒叫嚣的法官罗兰·弗莱斯勒（Roland Freisler）主持。

sentences.en: Many were humiliated before being sentenced to death by hanging, strangled slowly with piano wire.
sentences.zh: 许多人在被判处绞刑前受到羞辱，用钢琴线被缓慢勒死。

sentences.en: In total, some 7,000 people were arrested and almost 5,000 were executed, including the side-switching General Fromm, who was kept in prison for a year, only to be executed shortly before Germany’s surrender in 1945.
sentences.zh: 总计约有7,000人被捕，近5,000人被处决，其中包括倒戈的弗罗姆将军，他在监狱里关了一年，却在1945年德国投降前不久被处决。

sentences.en: And to this day, the plot has remained one of history’s great “what ifs”.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，这场阴谋仍然是历史上最伟大的“如果”之一。

sentences.en: After all, it's almost more surprising that the blast didn’t kill Hitler.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，爆炸居然没能炸死希特勒，这几乎更让人感到意外。

sentences.en: If von Stauffenberg had been able to prime both bombs instead of only one, it would almost certainly have killed him.
sentences.zh: 如果冯·施陶芬贝格当时引爆了两枚炸弹而不是一枚，几乎肯定能炸死他。

sentences.en: If the meeting had been held in a concrete bunker deep underground, like usual, instead of the venue being changed for a breezier, wooden room above ground, it would almost certainly have killed him, as the blast force would have been contained.
sentences.zh: 如果会议像往常一样在地下深处的混凝土掩体中举行，而不是为了更凉爽而将地点改在地上简易木屋里，爆炸的威力将被限制在内，几乎肯定能炸死他。

sentences.en: If Hitler hadn’t been leaning over the table, it would almost certainly have killed him.
sentences.zh: 如果希特勒当时没有俯身看地图，几乎肯定能炸死他。

sentences.en: And if Heinz Brandt hadn’t pushed the briefcase to one side, it would almost certainly have killed him.
sentences.zh: 如果海因茨·勃兰特没有把公文包推到一边，几乎肯定能炸死他。

sentences.en: And if Hitler had been killed in the blast, it seems highly probable that Operation Valkyrie would have proceeded as it was intended.
sentences.zh: 而且，如果希特勒在爆炸中身亡，“瓦尔基里行动”极有可能按原计划顺利进行。

sentences.en: The reserve army would have arrested the supposedly “disloyal” elements within the Nazi party.
sentences.zh: 后备军本会逮捕纳粹党内所谓的“不忠”分子。

sentences.en: Field Marshal Erwin von Witzleben would have become Commander-in-Chief; Germany may well have sought peace, and World War II might have ended in the summer of 1944.
sentences.zh: 埃尔温·冯·维茨莱本元帅会成为总司令；德国很可能会寻求和平，第二次世界大战也许就会在1944年夏天结束。

sentences.en: As you’ve heard, things didn’t work out that way, and the consequences were devastating.
sentences.zh: 正如你所听到的，事情并没有那样发展，其后果是毁灭性的。

sentences.en: Between that hot July afternoon in 1944 and the end of the war the following May, another six to eight million people would lose their lives.
sentences.zh: 从1944年那个炎热的七月下午到次年五月战争结束，又有六到八百万人的生命消逝。

sentences.en: If Hitler had died in the Wolf’s Lair that day, many of them might have been spared.
sentences.zh: 如果那天希特勒在“狼穴”丧命，其中许多人或许就能幸免于难。

sentences.en: Instead, the war raged on, and the failed coup of July 20th went down as one of history’s most haunting ‘what ifs’.
sentences.zh: 然而，战火仍在继续，7月20日的未遂政变作为历史上最令人挥之不去的“如果”之一载入了史册。

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode on Operation Valkyrie and the plot to kill Hitler.
sentences.zh: 好了，关于瓦尔基里行动和刺杀希特勒的阴谋，今天的节目就到这里。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 出品的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，注意安全，我们下期节目见。
